concern.concern: Fact F9 says that the constant function on Q has integral “Δμ(𝖸)=Δ” under a probability measure μ. For its inner-integral application μ = δ(y,·) is a measure on Q, so μ(𝖸) is generally undefined; the expression should use the underlying integration space. The intended constant-integral identity is elementary and the lower bound remains valid.

original_concerns.reason: Confirmed typed constant-integral error in F9. In Proof1.1 the measure is delta(y,·) on Q, so mu(Y) need not be defined and cannot represent its total mass. In Proof2.1 the outer measure is P on Y. The actual simple-integral Definition and probability Definition give Delta mu(S)=Delta on the measure’s own underlying space S. State that generic identity so both actual applications are typed. The original risk Statement, extended-risk/infinity case and choice-free argument remain sound.
